title: 1 Samuel 8–10; 13; 15–16
notes: Study aids companion for OT reading

footnotes.text: 1 Samuel 8:20. Nearly all the nations in the surrounding areas had kings. Before Samuel, Israel had experienced uneven leadership and disunity through the system of judges, which may have also contributed to their desire for a king (seeJudges 17:6;18:1;19:1;21:25).

See Kenneth L. Barker and others, eds.,NIV Study Bible: Fully Revised Edition(2020), 442, note on1 Samuel 10:5.

Examples include the New International Version, the New Living Translation, and the Christian Standard Bible. The Greek Septuagint also lists 3,000 chariots (see Robert Alter,The Hebrew Bible: A Translation with Commentary[2019], 2:223, note on1 Samuel 13:5).

See Adele Berlin and Marc Zvi Brettler, eds.,The Jewish Study Bible, 2nd ed. (2014), 569–70, note on1 Samuel 13:5. For more about large numbers in the Bible, see Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament, 126.
